svg.title: BitVM transaction graph — classic BitVM2 layout
svg.desc: Bitcoin transaction graph with input and output columns and per-input authorization types. Blue paths show operator transactions; red paths show challenges and timeouts. Dots mark connected branches; line crossings without dots are not connected.
svg.text: BitVM transaction graph — classic BitVM2 layout
Blue: operator / claim paths Red: challenge / timeout paths Gold dashes: protocol signals Dots mark connected branches
Labels beneath inputs show the sighash used by each transaction template, rather than every signature type a script might accept.
D and F: CSV · challenged claim
i0 / i1 …: template input indices; fee inputs are omitted.
ALL: commits to all outputs and, without ACP, all inputs.
NONE: commits to no outputs; the signature is still valid.
SINGLE|ACP: commits to this input and its same-index output.
ALL|ACP: commits to this input and all outputs.
ACP = ANYONECANPAY; labels omit the SIGHASH_ prefix.
—: no transaction signature; sighash does not apply.
WOTS signs data; scripts validate preimages, labels and evidence.
Watchtower-Timeout: W-j uses ALL; ACK-j uses NONE.
Deposit uses ECDSA ALL; other illustrated ALL signatures use Taproot.
Additional wallet and fee inputs require their own signatures.
j and k identify Watchtower and Verifier branches; each may repeat.
Spending D or F in a dispute or timeout prevents Take-2.
Fee outputs, P2A outputs, change and GOAT settlement are omitted.
PreKickoff slots and early challenges — G comes from Kickoff above; K-i funds its input
